issues.description: Bookend invariant (Start/End frame pairing) broken by race between timeout task, in-flight pushes, and overlapping invocations.
issues.detail: _output_response_open and _close_task are shared mutable state with no lock. The 1.0s timeout-driven End frame can fire while _push_text_frame is mid-await, and a second LLMContextFrame arriving during streaming can push a second Start without closing the first. State the invariant and serialize access, or drop the timer entirely and emit Start/End around the loop.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer raises JSONDecodeError, aborting the stream and leaving bookend state corrupted.
issues.detail: json.loads is called with no try/except. A malformed SSE line propagates out of process_frame mid-response, leaving _output_response_open=True and a dangling close task. Either document transformers as total (catch and return None) or wrap at the call site and log+skip. The transformer contract under malformed input must be stated.

issues.description: AWS bedrock-agentcore client is created and torn down per LLMContextFrame instead of once per processor lifetime.
issues.detail: async with self._aws_session.client(...) opens a fresh client on every frame. Boto session+client setup is non-trivial and adds per-frame latency. Open the client once in setup() and close it in cleanup() so client lifecycle stops leaking into the per-call hot path.

issues.description: No exception safety around AgentCore invocation; failures leave bookend state wedged for the next invocation.
issues.detail: If invoke_agent_runtime or any async-for iteration raises, Start may already be pushed, _output_response_open stays True, and _close_task remains scheduled. The next LLMContextFrame then pushes a second Start without closing the first. Wrap in try/finally that guarantees the bookend invariant on every failure path.

issues.description: Public parameter agentArn violates PEP 8 and the file's own snake_case convention.
issues.detail: Every other constructor parameter uses snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region) but agentArn is camelCase, mirroring the AWS field. Rename to agent_arn and translate to agentRuntimeArn at the boto3 call site. This is the signature users type; keep one convention at the Python boundary.

issues.description: Default context transformer silently swallows non-text content parts, masking malformed multimodal input.
issues.detail: ' '.join([part.get('text', '') for part in content]) emits empty strings for image/tool parts, producing leading/trailing/double spaces and silent omissions. Filter non-text parts then join, or document explicitly that only text parts are supported and refuse others. The postcondition is currently ambiguous.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a single verdict: the processor's framing state machine is under-specified and racy. The Start/End bookend invariant is held by unsynchronized mutable state, a 1s timeout task, and a final explicit close — three representations of the same fact that race with each other, with overlapping invocations, and with exceptions. The default response transformer can raise JSONDecodeError mid-stream and corrupt that state. The boto client lifecycle leaks into the per-frame path. Naming (agentArn) and the silent-drop multimodal default round out the cleanup list.
